Only a note whose latest HONOURED lifecycle op is still an accept is stranded: the walk (`RewindImpact.strandedAccepts(in:pastTarget:amendments:)`, which the rewind preview also counts — M4-RW-038) asks `AnnotationDeriver.isHonouredLifecycleOp`, so a Stet, reject, archive or reopen the writer put over the accept is their later answer and stands — a stetted note stays stetted with its reply, and a note they reopened is not reported as reopened by the rewind. Before #128 item 3 the walk hand-listed accept/reject/archive/revert without Stet or reopen, read the accept under a Stet as the latest answer and reverted the note to open over the writer's Stet

scope: PartialRestorePicker.restore / revertNotes (History's Revert here…, manuscript text)
statement: a checkpoint revert answers the accepted suggestions it takes back: each note `RewindImpact.strandedAccepts(in:revertedBy:through:amendments:)` names — the full rewind's list past the checkpoint's pointer, kept to the paragraphs the restore op writes — is reopened by a changes-free `.claudeAcceptRevert` stamped with the checkpoint id, appended right after the restore op and only when that op landed. A revert never removes a paragraph, so a stranded accept is always reopened, never archived; an accept on a paragraph the revert does not write keeps its text and stays accepted, and a Stet, reject, archive or reopen over the accept stands (the deriver's honoured-lifecycle rule). Both halves of RULING-28 come from one plan per document (`PartialRestorePicker.RevertPlan`): the sheet's confirm line ('N accepted suggestion(s) will be reopened on A, B.') before Revert and the sheet's result ('Reopened N accepted suggestion(s) on A, B.') after; a deleted (withdrawn) note still gets its revert in the log but is neither promised nor reported. Both halves ask one door (`splitByTheDoor`'s settled posture), so the promise and the act cannot count different documents. What does not land is NAMED, never only logged (RULING-52): a restore op that will not write says 'Not restored: A (why).' and reopens nothing; a reopen that will not write says 'Couldn't reopen N accepted suggestion(s) on A — still marked accepted.'; either keeps the sheet up. The reopen lines are built by `Restore.strandedAcceptReverts` and their append is a counted writer site (`manuscriptWriterCallSites`). An open document sees both text and status through the presenter re-read (`DocumentStore.reReadAfterExternalChange`). Not registered for ⌘Z, as no checkpoint revert is (plan 6c ruling Q-2). Before #128 item 2 the path did no stranded-accept handling: a revert to a checkpoint from before an accept left the note 'accepted' over text that no longer held the change, and the sheet named nothing
reachability: LIVE — History → a checkpoint row → Revert here…, over a suggestion accepted since that checkpoint
